adaptations.summary: The fork/ directory itself: manifest, sync routine, tests and the upgrade/AGPL/upstream-contribution documentation.
adaptations.why: We follow upstream and do not develop this product ourselves, so the fork needs a maintenance layer and that layer is by definition not upstream's. It is confined to one new top-level directory and modifies no upstream file, which keeps the merge surface at zero.

checks.reason: The sync routine is gone or renamed, so nothing is watching upstream any more.

Upstream has created its own fork/ directory, so our layer now collides with theirs and has to move.

adaptations.summary: Host-local docker-compose.override.yml on each deployment box, seeded from fork/templates/docker-compose.override.example.yml.
adaptations.why: Site-specific deployment settings (ports, volumes, resource limits, extra services) belong in Compose's own override mechanism, not in a patch to upstream's docker-compose.yml. The live file stays untracked because it is per host; the committed template is what we review and keep in step with upstream.

Upstream's compose file no longer declares a services block, so the override merges into nothing.
Upstream renamed or removed the app service. Compose merges overrides BY SERVICE NAME, so our override would silently stop applying instead of failing.
Upstream renamed or removed the cron service, so any override we carry for scheduled jobs silently stops applying.
Upstream stopped loading .env into the app service, so environment-variable adaptations (our tier 1 default) no longer reach the container.

adaptations.summary: Standalone SIE 8-year migration validation instrument (lib/import/sie-migration-validation.ts) used to check the Fortnox-to-Accounted migration, plus its tests.
adaptations.why: Wholly new files that touch no existing upstream file, so they carry no merge surface of their own. They are still a real difference from upstream and need both a local check and an upstream-absent check: an accidental revert and a future upstream file landing at the same path should both go red instead of silently disappearing.

adaptations.summary: docker/cron.Dockerfile invokes supercronic by its installed absolute path in ENTRYPOINT instead of relying on PATH.
adaptations.why: Container hardening, not a bug fix on the current image (see fork/DECISIONS.md, 2026-09-05): the image supplies a working PATH today, but an absolute ENTRYPOINT removes that runtime dependency entirely. Modifies an upstream file, so it is a genuine tier 2 patch. It landed directly on main rather than on a dedicated fork/patches branch, which is a documented deviation from the tier 2 procedure in fork/README.md section 4, not a template for future patches.

checks.reason: The absolute-path ENTRYPOINT hardening was reverted, so the image is back to depending on PATH to find supercronic.
The guard test for the absolute ENTRYPOINT is gone, so a future upstream merge could silently drop the hardening it exists to catch.

adaptations.summary: Underlagsjakt extension: the surface where Mattias answers bertil's underlagsjakt questions (bertil contract 1.1), enabled through extensions.config.json and upstream's generated extension registry.
adaptations.why: Mattias decision 2026-09-17: the answers belong in this backoffice, built as an extension rather than in core so every upstream catch-up stays mergeable. The code is wholly new files under extensions/general/underlagsjakt/ and components/extensions/general/. Enabling it goes through the sanctioned extension seam, which unavoidably touches upstream-owned files: extensions.config.json (one id appended), the committed registry under lib/extensions/_generated/ (regenerated by npm run setup:extensions, additive lines only), lib/extensions/__tests__/sectors.test.ts, which pins the number of enabled extensions and fails otherwise, and messages/sv.json plus messages/en.json, where i18n/__tests__/message-keys.test.ts requires every UI string to live (one new top-level `underlagsjakt` namespace, inserted mid-file before `extensions` so upstream's usual appends at the end do not touch the same lines). On an upstream merge that touches these files, keep upstream's lines, re-append the id, rerun setup:extensions and recount.
